page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.large is a shared-core virtual machine instance built on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features two vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512 and AES cryptography. The server provides 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include dedicated hardware accelerators or local disk storage, relying on network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate entry-level throughput influenced by shared CPU scheduling and modest core counts. Stress-ng evaluations indicate weak single-core performance at 1090.78 and multi-core output at 2067.18, aligning with the bottom tiers of tested systems. Geekbench assessments show comparable results, logging 939.0 in single-core and 1598.0 in multi-core metrics. Memory throughput drops significantly when exceeding cache boundaries, moving from 158.75 GB/sec in small cached reads to 16.93 GB/sec in large uncached reads and 13.99 GB/sec in write operations. Application benchmarks reflect these limitations, with static web serving reaching 2.32 GB/sec and PassMark database operations scoring 558.34, though Redis SET throughput maintains 2.58 million operations per second.

From an operational and resource perspective, the instance provides an economical entry point for lightweight services that do not require dedicated physical cores or intensive compute cycles. The primary tradeoff lies in shared CPU contention and baseline network limits, which cap sustained performance under heavy multi-threaded loads. As a result, Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.large is appropriate for basic web servers, development environments, low-traffic staging systems, and microservices requiring a balanced memory footprint without persistent compute intensity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.large is an entry-tier virtual instance configured with two shared vCPUs on a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the KVM hypervisor, it provides 8.0 GB of RAM, offering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory profile without local storage or GPU hardware. The CPU architecture supports AVX-512, though benchmark results position both single-core and multi-core compute throughput within lower percentiles, as observed in Geekbench and stress-ng results. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 16.93 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput caps at 2.32 GB/sec. Given its shared CPU model and absence of dedicated local storage, this instance is suited for lightweight workloads such as low-traffic web hosting, basic staging environments, light automation, and small-footprint background utilities.
